newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German chemical shares hit by Bayer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German chemical shares hit by Bayer.

text.p: German chemical shares went into a tailspin on Tuesday as investors reacted to a muted outlook from Bayer AG while still digesting last week's disappointing results from Hoechst AG.
"There is a definite malaise hitting the market and the chemicals in particular," said Penny Tattersall, analyst at CS First Boston in London.
Bayer AG led the decline of Germany's big three chemical companies by falling 4.3 percent to 68.7 marks in post-floor hours trade.
Hoechst, which reported its earnings last week and shocked markets by shelving plans to list its HMR drugs unit on the bourse, saw its shares drop 2.45 marks to 67.05.
BASF, the last of the three groups to report its core figures, saw shares ease 1.84 marks to 61.51, even though it reported a higher than expected dividend payout..

While analysts noted the decline occurred against the backdrop of a generally weak market, they also said the chemicals sector was partly to blame for the DAX index's 1.78 percent drop in floor trade.
Analysts said reasons for the sharp drop were two-fold.
Riding high on the benefits of an improved currency market position and a pickup in global economic growth, shares in German chemical groups fared very well during the first weeks of this year.

Analysts said the share market euphoria may have led to unrealistic expectations for 1996 results. "The market had even higher expectations than analysts did," said Ronald Koehler of BHF Bank in Frankfurt.

But analysts said the rapid share fall, foreshadowed last Tuesday when shares already dropped rapidly even though Hoechst and Bayer both reported a higher dividend and strong results, was triggered by the companies themselves.

For investors the outlook at Bayer, where management board chairman Manfred Schneider said sales could top 50 billion marks ($29.6 billion) and net profit would at least match 1996's 2.7 billion, was particularly subdued.
Even though Bayer is known to be cautious in its outlooks, analysts said the forecasts were unusually subdued.
"The outlook really floored the market," said CS First Boston's Tattersall.
Bayer executives said growth in Europe, still the group's largest market, could be slightly weaker than expected and there was little room to adjust prices.

It left open the chance it might experience another bout of currency market uncertainty, especially as talk about a possible delay to the launch of Europe's currency union tends to depress the dollar against the mark.
While analysts said these were all valid reasons for a slightly less bright outlook, the share slump caught the market off-guard.
Analysts were uniformly disappointed with Hoechst which posted a loss in the fourth quarter even though management had sounded very optimistic late in the year.
Hoechst's decision to reverse plans to list its drugs unit on the bourse also has a knock-on effect for its rivals.
After the Hoechst step, the market might perceive "that there is now less pressure to follow the demerger route," CS First Boston's Tattersall added.
Being the third large company to report its figures, BASF was seen by analysts as being hurt unfairly by the results of the other two companies, falling victim to generally poor market sentiment.
BASF announced it was raising its dividend for 1996 to 1.70 marks per share from 1.40 marks and that group net profit rose 12.9 percent to 2.79 billion marks ($1.7 billion) from 2.47 billion marks.

Pre-tax profit climbed 6.9 percent to 4.41 billion marks from 4.13 billion, above analysts' forecasts for a five percent rise on average. The dividend payout also beat forecasts for a figure of 1.60 marks.
Generally, however, analysts said the share market losses should not last very long, since the fundamental situation was still solid at the German chemicals groups.
"I think the market will realise the fundamental factors do not warrant this reaction," said BHF's Koehler.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.690 German Marks)
